full_judgment:
3. The Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakah (RAJUK) floated a tender notice inviting sale offer for the auction of commercial plots at Motijheel, Uttara and Sayedabad Commercial Areas as published in 'The Daily Inqilab" on 01.11.2005. The writ-petitioner-company participated in the auction for the purchase of three plots bearing Nos. 68, 70 and 72 each measuring ten kathas at Sonargaon Janapath, Sector-11, Uttara Commercial Area, Dhaka by depositing earnest money of Tk. 10,00000/- (ten lacs) for each plot. The offer of the writ-petitioner-company was 31.50 lacs for one katha making the offer of Tk. 3.15 crore for each of the 10 katha plots. After opening the tenders, the bids of the writ-petitioner were adjudged the highest and accordingly, RAJUK, vide its three memos dated 03.10.2006 allotted those plots in favour of the writ-petitioner pursuant to the decision taken in its “প্লট নিলাম বিক্রয় কমিটি”(Plot Auction Sale Committee). By the above memos, the writ-petitioner was asked to pay the remaining amount of the bids money and other charges within 2 (two) months. Because of its financial difficulties, the writ petitioner by letter dated 26.11.2006 prayed for extension of time for a further period of six months. Writ respondent-RAJUK, however, sat over such prayer without taking any decision and subsequently, the writ-petitioner wrote to RAJUK seeking permission to pay the entire balance amount and to get registration of those plots. Finally, the writ-petitioner came to know that the allotment of the plots was cancelled by RAJUK, although no formal information was sent to the writ-petitioner in this regard. Against this backdrop, since RAJUK published the impugned tender in respect of the self-same plots, the writ-petitioner-company moved the High Court Division by filing writ petitions and obtained Rules Nisi and supplementary Rules in Writ Petition Nos. 5167, 5168 and 5169 of 2008. 

 6. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, writ-respondents have filed instant Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 3118-3120 of 2012 before this Division and leave was granted to all the civil petitions on 07.04.2013 resulting in Civil Appeal Nos. 57-59 of 2013.
